source: It should not have been omitted that previous to completely stripping the body of the leviathan, he was beheaded. Now, the beheading of the Sperm Whale is a scientific anatomical feat, upon which experienced whale surgeons very much pride themselves: and not without reason.

Consider that the whale has nothing that can properly be called a neck; on the contrary, where his head and body seem to join, there, in that very place, is the thickest part of him. Remember, also, that the surgeon must operate from above, some eight or ten feet intervening between him and his subject, and that subject almost hidden in a discoloured, rolling, and oftentimes tumultuous and bursting sea. Bear in mind, too, that under these untoward circumstances he has to cut many feet deep in the flesh; and in that subterraneous manner, without so much as getting one single peep into the ever-contracting gash thus made, he must skilfully steer clear of all adjacent, interdicted parts, and exactly divide the spine at a critical point hard by its insertion into the skull. Do you not marvel, then, at Stubb’s boast, that he demanded but ten minutes to behead a sperm whale?

When first severed, the head is dropped astern and held there by a cable till the body is stripped. That done, if it belong to a small whale it is hoisted on deck to be deliberately disposed of. But, with a full grown leviathan this is impossible; for the sperm whale’s head embraces nearly one third of his entire bulk, and completely to suspend such a burden as that, even by the immense tackles of a whaler, this were as vain a thing as to attempt weighing a Dutch barn in jewellers’ scales.

The Pequod’s whale being decapitated and the body stripped, the head was hoisted against the ship’s side—about half way out of the sea, so that it might yet in great part be buoyed up by its native element. And there with the strained craft steeply leaning over to it, by reason of the enormous downward drag from the lower mast-head, and every yard-arm on that side projecting like a crane over the waves; there, that blood-dripping head hung to the Pequod’s waist like the giant Holofernes’s from the girdle of Judith.

When this last task was accomplished it was noon, and the seamen went below to their dinner. Silence reigned over the before tumultuous but now deserted deck. An intense copper calm, like a universal yellow lotus, was more and more unfolding its noiseless measureless leaves upon the sea.

A short space elapsed, and up into this noiselessness came Ahab alone from his cabin. Taking a few turns on the quarter-deck, he paused to gaze over the side, then slowly getting into the main-chains he took Stubb’s long spade—still remaining there after the whale’s decapitation—and striking it into the lower part of the half-suspended mass, placed its other end crutch-wise under one arm, and so stood leaning over with eyes attentively fixed on this head.

It was a black and hooded head; and hanging there in the midst of so intense a calm, it seemed the Sphynx’s in the desert. “Speak, thou vast and venerable head,” muttered Ahab, “which, though ungarnished with a beard, yet here and there lookest hoary with mosses; speak, mighty head, and tell us the secret thing that is in thee. Of all divers, thou hast dived the deepest. That head upon which the upper sun now gleams, has moved amid this world’s foundations. Where unrecorded names and navies rust, and untold hopes and anchors rot; where in her murderous hold this frigate earth is ballasted with bones of millions of the drowned; there, in that awful water-land, there was thy most familiar home. Thou hast been where bell or diver never went; hast slept by many a sailor’s side, where sleepless mothers would give their lives to lay them down. Thou saw’st the locked lovers when leaping from their flaming ship; heart to heart they sank beneath the exulting wave; true to each other, when heaven seemed false to them. Thou saw’st the murdered mate when tossed by pirates from the midnight deck; for hours he fell into the deeper midnight of the insatiate maw; and his murderers still sailed on unharmed—while swift lightnings shivered the neighboring ship that would have borne a righteous husband to outstretched, longing arms. O head! thou hast seen enough to split the planets and make an infidel of Abraham, and not one syllable is thine!”
“Sail ho!” cried a triumphant voice from the main-mast-head.

“Aye? Well, now, that’s cheering,” cried Ahab, suddenly erecting himself, while whole thunder-clouds swept aside from his brow. “That lively cry upon this deadly calm might almost convert a better man.—Where away?”
“Three points on the starboard bow, sir, and bringing down her breeze to us!

“Better and better, man. Would now St. Paul would come along that way, and to my breezelessness bring his breeze! O Nature, and O soul of man! how far beyond all utterance are your linked analogies! not the smallest atom stirs or lives on matter, but has its cunning duplicate in mind.”

paragraphs: It should not have been omitted that before the body of the leviathan was completely stripped, he was beheaded. Now, the beheading of the Sperm Whale is a scientific anatomical feat upon which experienced whale surgeons very much pride themselves — and not without reason.

Consider that the whale has nothing that can properly be called a neck; on the contrary, where his head and body seem to join, there, in that very place, is the thickest part of him. Remember, too, that the surgeon must operate from above, with some eight or ten feet between him and his subject, and that subject almost hidden in a discolored, rolling, and often tumultuous and bursting sea. Bear in mind also that under these unfavorable circumstances he has to cut many feet deep into the flesh; and in that underground fashion, without getting so much as a single peep into the ever-contracting gash he is making, he must skillfully steer clear of all the neighboring, forbidden parts, and divide the spine exactly at a critical point close to where it enters the skull. Don't you marvel, then, at Stubb's boast that he needed only ten minutes to behead a sperm whale?

When first severed, the head is dropped astern and held there by a cable until the body is stripped. That done, if it belongs to a small whale, it is hoisted on deck to be dealt with at leisure. But with a full-grown leviathan this is impossible; for the sperm whale's head makes up nearly one third of his entire bulk, and to suspend such a burden completely, even by the immense tackles of a whaler, would be as futile as trying to weigh a Dutch barn in jewelers' scales.

The Pequod's whale having been beheaded and the body stripped, the head was hoisted against the ship's side — about halfway out of the sea, so that it might still be largely buoyed up by its native element. And there, with the strained vessel leaning steeply over toward it because of the enormous downward drag from the lower masthead, and every yard-arm on that side sticking out like a crane over the waves — there that blood-dripping head hung at the Pequod's waist like the giant Holofernes's from the girdle of Judith.

A short time passed, and up into this silence came Ahab, alone, from his cabin. Taking a few turns on the quarter-deck, he paused to gaze over the side; then, slowly climbing into the main-chains, he took Stubb's long spade — still lying there after the whale's beheading — and, striking it into the lower part of the half-suspended mass, he placed its other end like a crutch under one arm, and so stood leaning over, his eyes intently fixed on this head.

It was a black and hooded head; and hanging there in the midst of so intense a calm, it seemed like the Sphynx's in the desert. Of all divers, you have dived the deepest. That head upon which the upper sun now gleams has moved among this world's foundations. Where unrecorded names and navies rust, and untold hopes and anchors rot; where in her murderous hold this frigate earth is ballasted with the bones of millions of the drowned; there, in that awful water-land, there was your most familiar home. You have been where diving-bell or diver never went; you have slept by many a sailor's side, where sleepless mothers would give their lives to lay them down. You saw the locked lovers when they leaped from their flaming ship; heart to heart they sank beneath the exulting wave; true to each other, when heaven seemed false to them. "Sail ho!" cried a triumphant voice from the main-masthead.

"Better and better, man. If only St. Paul would come along that way now, and bring his breeze to my breezelessness! O Nature, and O soul of man! how far beyond all words are your linked analogies! Not the smallest atom stirs or lives on matter without having its cunning duplicate in mind."

modern_da.title: Kapitel 70 — Sfinksen
paragraphs: Det skulle ikke have været udeladt, at leviatanen blev halshugget, før kroppen var helt flået. Nu er halshugningen af kaskelotten en videnskabelig anatomisk bedrift, som erfarne hvalkirurger er meget stolte af — og ikke uden grund.

Tænk på, at hvalen ikke har noget, man ordentligt kan kalde en hals. Tværtimod er det lige dér, hvor hans hoved og krop synes at mødes, at han er tykkest. Husk også, at kirurgen må operere oppefra, med otte eller ti fod mellem sig selv og sit emne, og at emnet er næsten skjult i et misfarvet, rullende og ofte stormfuldt og bølgende hav. Husk også, at han under disse ugunstige forhold må skære mange fod ned i kødet. Og på denne underjordiske måde, uden så meget som at få et eneste kig ind i det stadig lukkende sår, han laver, må han dygtigt styre uden om alle de nærliggende, forbudte dele og dele rygsøjlen nøjagtigt på et kritisk punkt tæt ved, hvor den går ind i kraniet. Undrer du dig så ikke over Stubbs pral om, at han kun brugte ti minutter på at halshugge en kaskelot?

Når hovedet først er skåret af, lader man det falde agterud og holder det dér med et tov, til kroppen er flået. Når det er gjort, hejser man det, hvis det hører til en lille hval, op på dækket for at tage sig af det i ro og mag. Men med en fuldvoksen leviatan er det umuligt. For kaskelottens hoved udgør næsten en tredjedel af hele hans omfang, og at hænge så stor en byrde helt op, selv i hvalfangerens uhyre taljer, ville være lige så nytteløst som at prøve at veje en hollandsk lade på guldsmedens vægt.

Da Pequods hval var halshugget og kroppen flået, blev hovedet hejst op langs skibssiden — omtrent halvvejs ud af havet, så det stadig for en stor del kunne bæres af sit eget element. Og dér, mens det anstrengte skib lå stejlt over mod det på grund af det enorme træk nedad fra det nederste mastehoved, og hver eneste rånok på den side stak ud som en kran over bølgerne — dér hang det bloddryppende hoved ved Pequods liv som den kæmpe Holofernes' hoved fra Judiths bælte.

Da dette sidste arbejde var gjort, var det middag, og sømændene gik ned for at spise. Stilhed lagde sig over dækket, der et øjeblik før havde været så larmende og nu lå øde. En intens kobberfarvet vindstille, som en altomfattende gul lotus, foldede mere og mere af sine tavse, grænseløse blade ud over havet.

Der gik et kort stykke tid, og op i denne stilhed kom Ahab, alene, fra sin kahyt. Han gik nogle ture på agterdækket, standsede for at se ud over rælingen, og klatrede så langsomt op i storevantet, tog Stubbs lange spade — som stadig lå dér efter hvalens halshugning — og stak den ind i den nederste del af den halvt hængende masse, satte dens anden ende som en krykke ind under den ene arm og stod sådan og lænede sig ud med øjnene stift rettet mod dette hoved.

Det var et sort hoved med hætte, og som det hang dér midt i den dybe ro, lignede det Sfinksen i ørkenen. »Tal, du vældige, ærværdige hoved,« mumlede Ahab, »du, som ikke har noget skæg og alligevel her og der ser gråhåret ud af mos. Tal, mægtige hoved, og fortæl os den hemmelighed, du gemmer på. Af alle dykkere har du dykket dybest. Det hoved, som den øvre sol nu skinner på, har bevæget sig mellem verdens grundpiller. Dér hvor navne og flåder, der aldrig blev nedskrevet, ruster, og utallige håb og ankre rådner; dér hvor denne fregat, jorden, i sit morderiske lastrum er ballasteret med knoglerne af millioner af druknede; dér, i det forfærdelige vandland, var dit allermest kendte hjem. Du har været, hvor ingen dykkerklokke eller dykker nogensinde kom; du har sovet ved siden af mange en sømand, hvor søvnløse mødre ville give deres liv for at lægge sig ned. Du så de forelskede, der var låst i hinandens arme, da de sprang fra deres brændende skib; hjerte mod hjerte sank de under den jublende bølge, tro mod hinanden, da himlen syntes utro mod dem. Du så den myrdede styrmand, da sørøverne kastede ham ud fra dækket midt om natten; i timevis faldt han ned i den dybere midnat i det umættelige gab, og hans mordere sejlede ufortrødent videre — mens et hurtigt lyn splintrede det nærliggende skib, som ville have båret en retskaffen ægtemand hen til udstrakte, længselsfulde arme. O hoved! Du har set nok til at sprænge planeterne og gøre Abraham til vantro, og ikke en eneste stavelse kommer fra dig!«
»Sejl ho!« råbte en triumferende stemme fra stormastens top.

»Ja? Nå, det er da opmuntrende,« råbte Ahab og rettede sig pludselig op, mens hele tordenskyer drog væk fra hans pande. »Det livlige råb i den dødelige vindstille kunne næsten omvende en bedre mand. — Hvor henne?«
»Tre streger på styrbord bov, hr., og hun bringer sin brise ned til os!«

»Bedre og bedre, mand. Bare Sankt Paulus ville komme den vej nu og bringe sin brise til min vindstille! O natur, og o menneskets sjæl! Hvor langt hinsides alle ord er jeres forbundne ligheder! Ikke det mindste atom rører sig eller lever i stoffet uden at have sin snedige dobbeltgænger i sindet.«
